- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- When the history shows a sharp spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots immediately after, then corrects downward — adjust for lagged correction.
- Model underestimates when true values show strong downward momentum (e.g., 85→75 range) — increase baseline by 1–2 points for such trends.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day windows — if forecast is >85, reduce by 1–3 points for next 5 days; if <80, increase by 1–2 points.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are above 84, don’t assume next day will stay above 84; cap at 84–85 unless strong bullish signal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “bottom” of a downtrend — add 1–2 points to forecast if true outcome is below 75 and history shows clear decline.
- If model forecast is >85 and true outcome is <80, reduce forecast by 5–10 points to avoid overconfidence in upside momentum.
